prompt: Write a retry helper: call a Flaky task up to maxAttempts times, return the first success, and if every attempt throws, rethrow the LAST exception wrapped in a RuntimeException.
explanation: The try/catch lives INSIDE the loop: a successful attempt() returns straight out of the method, while a failure is caught, stored in a variable declared before the loop, and the loop moves on to the next attempt. Each new failure overwrites the variable, so after the loop it necessarily holds the last exception, which is passed to new RuntimeException(cause) -- exception chaining that keeps the original failure reachable through getCause(). Wrapping also converts the checked Exception into an unchecked one, which is why retry needs no throws clause.
hints: Declare Exception last = null; before the loop so the variable outlives each iteration.
Inside the loop: try { return task.attempt(); } catch (Exception e) { last = e; } -- returning on success ends the retrying instantly.
Code after the loop only runs when every attempt failed, so throw there, handing the stored exception to the RuntimeException(Throwable) constructor that sets the cause.
